# Purpose of Falcon Dash

## What Falcon Dash is

Falcon Dash is a standalone, self-hostable operator dashboard for OpenClaw. It gives people a single place to understand what their agents are doing, manage Work, review sensitive actions, configure gateway-backed capabilities, browse agent files, schedule recurring work, and manage credentials.

Falcon Dash and the OpenClaw Gateway run on the same host and communicate over loopback or a host-local container network. Connecting Falcon Dash to a gateway on another machine is outside the supported product scope.

## The problem it solves

OpenClaw exposes a capable agent runtime, gateway protocol, configuration model, and operational
tools. Using those capabilities directly often requires familiarity with terminals, configuration
files, gateway RPC, and the host filesystem.

Falcon Dash makes that runtime operable through a cohesive web interface. It does not replace
OpenClaw or create a second source of runtime truth. It presents OpenClaw capabilities in an
operator-friendly form and adds the Falcon Dash Work domain for planning, governance, provenance,
and operational follow-through.

The default surface is Work: an executive view of what agents are doing, what needs the operator's
call, what is at risk, and what changed recently.

## Where it sits in the stack

```text
Operator
  |
  v
Falcon Dash  ----  standalone web dashboard and Work system
  |
  v
OpenClaw Gateway  ----  agent runtime, sessions, events, and native automation
  |
  v
AI Agent(s)  ----  agents, tools, and workspaces
```

Falcon Dash requires a co-resident OpenClaw Gateway and suitable gateway credentials. Everything
around that local core path is deployment choice: bare-metal or containerized installation,
reverse proxy, access control, tunnel, monitoring, DNS, and provisioning automation.

Fredbot Backend is one optional deployment integration. It can provision and operate Falcon Dash
for Fredbot-managed environments, but it is not part of Falcon Dash's required runtime architecture,
installation path, product identity, or source of truth.

## Product boundaries

- **OpenClaw owns the agent runtime.** Gateway behavior, agent processes, sessions, pairing, native
  cron execution, Run history, and the plugin SDK remain OpenClaw responsibilities.
- **Falcon Dash owns the operator experience and Work domain.** It owns the dashboard, semantic Work
  records and commands, operator workflows, local Work persistence, and Falcon-specific views.
- **Plugins extend the gateway without forking it.** Falcon-specific channel, prompt-context, or
  canvas behavior belongs in a versioned OpenClaw plugin. Core OpenClaw capabilities should continue
  to use the native gateway protocol.
- **Deployment tooling remains optional.** Hosting backends may install, configure, secure, monitor,
  and upgrade Falcon Dash, but the product must not depend on any one provider's control plane.
- **The gateway is local.** Falcon Dash supports a co-resident OpenClaw Gateway over loopback or a
  same-host container network. Cross-host gateway connectivity is intentionally out of scope.

## Design philosophy

The operator may also be the administrator, but Falcon Dash should not require infrastructure
expertise for ordinary use. Advanced controls remain available without dominating the default
workflow.

Key principles:

- **Installable by anyone.** Setup and documentation must support independent self-hosters, teams,
  and service providers without assuming Fredbot-managed infrastructure.
- **OpenClaw-native.** Falcon Dash composes with OpenClaw's protocol and plugin system instead of
  duplicating or forking gateway behavior.
- **Work first.** The primary view answers what is happening, what needs attention, what is blocked,
  and what changed.
- **Non-technical operators first.** Common actions use clear language and sensible defaults;
  specialist controls remain discoverable when needed.
- **Expose capabilities while preserving security.** Device pairing, approvals, scoped credentials,
  provenance, and authority boundaries must remain explicit.
- **Live and resilient.** Operators receive current gateway state and events, while failures and
  unavailable integrations degrade visibly instead of inventing healthy state.
- **Deployment-neutral.** Product behavior must not assume a particular cloud, tunnel, identity
  provider, monitoring stack, CRM, or provisioning backend.

## Who it is for

Falcon Dash is for anyone operating OpenClaw agents: individual self-hosters, technical and
non-technical operators, internal teams, consultants, managed-service providers, and hosting
platforms. Some will install and administer it themselves; others will use an installation managed
by a provider. Both are first-class product paths.
